consensus_summary: Mainstream Christian consensus identifies marriage/bride primarily as the covenantal union between Christ (bridegroom) and the Church/people of God (bride), rooted in OT Israel-as-wife-of-YHWH imagery and culminating in eschatological consummation; alternatives (individual soul, New Jerusalem as city, dispensational Israel/Church split, etc.) are secondary refinements.
book_summary: Covenant union of God and His people as a one-flesh bond in which the wife receives the Husband's Name and comes under His covering; opposite is divorce.
consensus_core_identification: Covenantal marriage union of God/Christ with His people (Church/Israel) as bride.
book_core_identification: Covenant union of God and His people as one-flesh bridal bond (Name + covering).
boundary_disagreement: None material; book adds one-flesh/Name/covering language and Divorce opposite without excluding consensus cases or adding alien ones.
rationale: Both reduce to the same central referent (God/Christ–people covenant marriage). Book's extra precision (one-flesh, Name reception, covering) and opposite are compatible elaborations already latent in the shared texts (Gen 2:24; Ezek 16:8; Eph 5; Rev 19), not a narrowed, broadened, or replaced core.
strongest_objection: Book's emphasis on 'receives the Husband's Name' and explicit Divorce opposite could be read as slightly more legal/covenantal than some mystical or purely ecclesiological framings, yet still within the consensus envelope.
